thread:
nina: Quick sync on checksum / manifest interop. We need a minimal, non-crypto checksum and a manifest layout that works for safetensors and sharded bundles. Draft idea: per-chunk adler32, 64KiB chunk size, small sidecar JSON named <model>.shard.manifest.json. Thoughts?

raj: Adler32 seems fine for detecting transfer corruption; keep SHA256 optional for signed releases. Important: manifest must encode compression mapping if shards are gzipped so chunk boundaries are meaningful.

hugo: Agree on 64KiB default. One question: how do loaders behave when manifest missing? My vote: conservative default = fail fast (strict), but allow cluster override to permit permissive behavior for latency-sensitive routes. Document fallback clearly.

nina: Good. Proposal: manifest fields = {format, chunk_size, checksum_algo, checksums:[...], partial_policy}. partial_policy = strict | permissive | zero_fill. If missing manifest, loader uses strict unless config allow_partial_missing_manifest=true.

raj: Also add model-level annotation "quant_sensitive": true so runtime can disallow permissive for those models. And telemetry: emit manifest.present boolean and partial_chunks_count.

hugo: Repair coordination: leader election per-shard using a lightweight lease in the local metadata store. Add backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd. Also cap concurrent repairs per-node.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: loader-manifest-v1 rollout 2026-04-03T02:00Z to us-west-2.

nina: Action items: 1) I'll draft manifest schema and examples including compressed-case mapping, 2) raj please add model annotation fields and telemetry keys, 3) hugo please sketch leader lease pseudocode and backoff parameters. We'll default to strict for canary.

raj: I'll also add a quick compatibility table: older safetensors without sidecar -> strict; bundles produced by our packager will include manifest.

hugo: I'll prototype a small test harness that simulates mid-read truncation and verifies both strict and permissive flows.

nina: Thanks all — will post the manifest PR later today. :thumbsup:
